title: Optimistic prefill arbiter: model scoring, kernel matching, and staged fallback
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an optimistic prefill arbiter thatfan-outs lightweight prefill probes to candidate model variants and selects the fastest acceptable candidate at decode time using a composite model+kernel score. The arbiter should improve median tail latency for short-turn interactions while preserving response quality and providing safe, observable fallbacks.

Background: We currently have multiple candidate model variants per request (full fp16, int8-quantized, trimmed KV-cache variant), and several kernel implementations (flash-attn, fused-causal, fallback CUDA kernels). Selecting the best backend at request time is nontrivial: kernel capability, sequence-length distribution, and current GPU headroom all affect real-world latency. Speculative decode techniques can help if we accept occasional rollbacks with safe fallback policies.

Proposal summary:
1) Candidate probe: on prefill, dispatch a small probe (2-8 tokens) to 1-3 candidate model+kernel pairs. Probes run with strict CPU/GPU scheduling priority and a short soft timeout (default 30ms).
2) Composite scoring: compute a kernel-match score composed of:
   - latency_est (model+kernel average latency estimate) weighted 0.5
   - memory_headroom_penalty (OOM risk heuristic) weighted 0.2
   - quant_compat_score (compatibility with request features: sampling, logits-scaling) weighted 0.15
   - acceptance_quality_signal (probe log-likelihood delta vs baseline) weighted 0.15
3) Acceptance metrics: a candidate is accepted if:
   - probe_likelihood_delta >= -0.25 nats per token (configurable), AND
   - normalized_kernel_match_score <= threshold_t (adaptive by SLAs), AND
   - no critical errors (OOM, CUDA kernel error).
4) Fallback orchestration: if accepted candidate fails mid-decode (OOM, kernel crash, or quality regression detected), automatically switch to the next best candidate with preserved KV cache where possible. If switching requires model change that invalidates KV cache, trigger a short re-prefill path with cached prompt embedding and apply token-level reconciliation heuristics (prefix-preserve + soft-rescore).
5) Rollout & controls: enable per-tenant flags (console toggle) with canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Automated rollback if QA metrics degrade beyond 2% in latency p50/p95 or 1% rise in perplexity on eval set.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit candidate_event proto with fields (candidate_id, kernel_fingerprint, composite_score, probe_latency_ms, probe_likelihood_delta, decision, fallback_reason).
- Add console dashboard: per-route acceptance_rate, fallback_rate, median_probe_latency, kernel_choice_distribution.
- Trace correlation: include probe_id in the top-level request trace and surface in traces UI.

Performance targets:
- Median latency improvement for small (<=64 token) responses: >= 12% on CPU-bound cases, >= 6% on GPU-bound cases.
- Fallback rate <= 3% on stable workloads.
- No more than 0.5% absolute degradation in subjective quality (eval-based) during canary.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for composite scoring and acceptance thresholds.
- Integration harness: simulate mixed workload with synthetic prompt distribution and run end-to-end traffic replay comparing baseline routing to arbiter.
- Shadow rollout for 2 weeks: log decisions without effecting production route; compute expected benefit and edge cases.

Design trade-offs & open questions:
- Probe cost vs benefit: probes add extra token compute; need to quantify break-even for different request mixes. Suggest running A/B on 20k requests to capture token-cost delta.
- KV cache preservation: switching models that have different kv-layouts forces re-prefill; evaluate whether small re-prefill penalties negate latency wins.
- Acceptance metric tuning: currently use likelihood-delta but in multi-turn conversation, per-token LL is noisy; consider embedding-similarity on first generated tokens as alternative.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: proto/events and score calculator + unit tests.
- Week 2: probe executor + kernel fingerprint registry + CLI flags.
- Week 3: fallback orchestrator with KV reconciliation heuristics.
- Week 4: shadow rollout + dashboards + runbook.
